videos.script: One bicycle ride, written down three ways. {{one-ride}} As a row in the app's database, with four columns and a type for each. As the event the app sends, with names and values nested inside each other. And as an email from the customer: Rua XV, twelve minutes, a dock that would not let go. {{three-ways}} Most people sort these by the file: a table, a JSON file, some text. {{wrong}} That is the wrong question. The right one is where the schema lives. {{question}} In the table, declared before any row arrives. In every record, travelling with it. Or nowhere at all, so somebody has to read the words. {{where}} Each answer moves a cost, to a check at the door or a check in every reader. {{cost}} In this lesson you watch each one happen. A table refuses a bad value. Nested events are flattened into rows. {{flatten}} A new version of the app changes a field and tells nobody. {{drift}} And a pattern finds station names in emails, and misses some of them. {{emails}} By the end you can look at any data and ask the useful question: who checks its shape, and when? {{end}}
